questions.question: A company needs to design a multi-region VPC architecture that supports 50,000 IP addresses per region with room for 100% growth. The design must avoid CIDR overlap and support hub-and-spoke connectivity. What CIDR allocation strategy should be used?
options: Use /16 CIDR blocks (10.0.0.0/16, 10.1.0.0/16) with /24 subnets
Use /15 CIDR blocks (10.0.0.0/15, 10.2.0.0/15) with /22 subnets
Use /14 CIDR blocks (10.0.0.0/14, 10.4.0.0/14) with /20 subnets
Use /13 CIDR blocks (10.0.0.0/13, 10.8.0.0/13) with /18 subnets
questions.explanation: A /14 CIDR provides 262,144 IP addresses (4x /16), allowing for 50,000 IPs plus 100% growth with significant headroom. Non-overlapping /14 blocks (10.0.0.0/14, 10.4.0.0/14) ensure no conflicts. /20 subnets provide 4,096 IPs each for proper segmentation.

questions.question: An enterprise requires a hybrid network design connecting 20 branch offices to AWS across 3 regions. Each branch needs 1 Gbps bandwidth with 99.9% availability. The solution must support dynamic routing and traffic engineering. What architecture provides the most cost-effective solution?
options: Direct Connect with multiple VIFs per location and BGP communities
Transit Gateway with Site-to-Site VPN using BGP and ECMP
SD-WAN solution with Transit Gateway Connect attachments
VPN CloudHub with multiple customer gateways per branch
questions.explanation: SD-WAN with Transit Gateway Connect provides dynamic routing, traffic engineering, and cost optimization by using internet connectivity while maintaining enterprise-grade features. It supports BGP, ECMP, and can achieve 99.9% availability with proper design.

questions.question: A company needs to design subnets for a 3-tier web application in a VPC with CIDR 10.0.0.0/16. The application requires public subnets for load balancers, private subnets for application servers, and database subnets. What subnet design follows AWS best practices?
questions.explanation: Using /20 subnets provides 4,096 IPs each, allowing for growth. This design follows AWS best practices by allocating larger blocks for different tiers and avoiding overlapping CIDR ranges.

questions.question: A financial services company requires network segmentation with strict isolation between environments. The design must support development, staging, and production with no cross-environment communication. Which Transit Gateway design pattern should be implemented?
options: Single Transit Gateway with multiple route tables and no route propagation
Separate Transit Gateways per environment with no peering
Single Transit Gateway with security groups controlling access
Multiple Transit Gateways with selective peering connections
questions.explanation: Separate Transit Gateways per environment provide complete network isolation, which is essential for financial services compliance. This prevents any possibility of cross-environment communication at the network layer.

questions.question: A global company needs to design a network architecture supporting 100 VPCs across 5 AWS regions with centralized internet egress and inspection. The solution must minimize latency and support 10 Gbps aggregate throughput. What architecture should be implemented?
options: Regional Transit Gateways with inter-region peering and centralized NAT Gateways
Global Transit Gateway with centralized inspection VPC and AWS Network Firewall
Regional inspection VPCs with Transit Gateway and Network Firewall per region
CloudWAN with centralized core network and regional inspection points
questions.explanation: Regional inspection VPCs minimize latency by keeping traffic local to each region while providing centralized control. Network Firewall can handle 10+ Gbps throughput per AZ, and Transit Gateway enables efficient routing.

questions.question: An organization needs to design IPv6 connectivity for their AWS infrastructure while maintaining IPv4 compatibility. The design must support 1000 subnets with automatic address assignment. What approach should be used?
options: IPv6-only VPC with NAT64 for IPv4 compatibility
Separate IPv4 and IPv6 VPCs with VPC peering
IPv4 VPC with IPv6 overlay using tunneling
Dual-stack VPC with /56 IPv6 CIDR and /64 subnets
questions.explanation: Dual-stack VPC with /56 IPv6 CIDR provides 256 /64 subnets, which can be expanded. This maintains IPv4 compatibility while enabling native IPv6 support with automatic address assignment.

questions.question: A startup needs to design a cost-effective network architecture for their web application that expects variable traffic patterns. The application requires high availability across 2 AZs. What load balancer configuration is most appropriate?
options: Network Load Balancer with cross-zone load balancing disabled
Application Load Balancer with cross-zone load balancing enabled
Gateway Load Balancer with health checks
Classic Load Balancer with sticky sessions
questions.explanation: Application Load Balancer is cost-effective for HTTP/HTTPS traffic with variable patterns. Cross-zone load balancing ensures even distribution across AZs for high availability.

questions.question: A media company requires a CDN solution that supports real-time streaming with sub-100ms latency globally. The solution must integrate with AWS services and support custom SSL certificates. What architecture should be designed?
options: Global Accelerator with Network Load Balancers and SSL termination
CloudFront with real-time streaming and AWS Certificate Manager
Multi-region Application Load Balancers with Route 53 latency routing
CloudFront with Lambda@Edge and custom SSL certificates
questions.explanation: CloudFront with Lambda@Edge provides the lowest latency for global content delivery and supports real-time streaming. Custom SSL certificates can be uploaded to CloudFront for brand requirements.

questions.question: A healthcare organization needs to design a network that complies with HIPAA requirements. The design must ensure data encryption in transit and at rest, with audit logging. Which components are essential?
options: VPC with default encryption, CloudTrail, and VPC Flow Logs
Private subnets, TLS 1.2+, AWS Config, and CloudTrail
NAT Gateways, security groups, and CloudWatch
Internet Gateway, NACLs, and AWS Shield
questions.explanation: HIPAA compliance requires private subnets for PHI, TLS 1.2+ for encryption in transit, AWS Config for compliance monitoring, and CloudTrail for audit logging of all API calls.

questions.question: A company wants to design a VPC that supports both public-facing web servers and private database servers. The database servers should not have internet access. What subnet design is appropriate?
options: Public subnets for web servers, private subnets with NAT Gateway for databases
Public subnets for web servers, private subnets without NAT Gateway for databases
All resources in public subnets with security groups controlling access
Private subnets for all resources with Application Load Balancer in public subnets
questions.explanation: Web servers need public subnets for internet access. Database servers should be in private subnets without NAT Gateway to prevent any internet access, following security best practices.

questions.question: An enterprise needs to design a network architecture that supports 500 Gbps of bandwidth between on-premises and AWS with sub-10ms latency. The solution must provide redundancy and support BGP routing policies. What design should be implemented?
options: Direct Connect Gateway with multiple 10G connections and ECMP
Site-to-Site VPN with multiple tunnels and BGP
AWS Outposts with local connectivity
Multiple 100G Direct Connect connections with LAG and BGP communities
questions.explanation: Multiple 100G Direct Connect connections can provide 500+ Gbps bandwidth. LAG provides redundancy and load distribution, while BGP communities enable advanced routing policies for traffic engineering.

questions.question: A SaaS company needs to design a multi-tenant network architecture where each tenant's traffic is isolated. The solution must scale to 1000 tenants and support centralized monitoring. What approach should be used?
options: Separate VPCs per tenant with VPC peering
Single VPC with tenant-specific subnets and security groups
Transit Gateway with separate route tables per tenant
Multiple AWS accounts with cross-account roles
questions.explanation: Transit Gateway with separate route tables per tenant provides scalable isolation while maintaining centralized management. This approach can scale to 1000+ tenants with proper route table design.

questions.question: A development team needs to design a network for a microservices application with 20 services. Each service needs to communicate with others securely. What service discovery and networking approach is most suitable?
options: Application Load Balancer with target groups per service
AWS Cloud Map with VPC Lattice for service-to-service communication
Network Load Balancer with static IP addresses
Route 53 private hosted zones with A records
questions.explanation: AWS Cloud Map provides service discovery for microservices, while VPC Lattice enables secure service-to-service communication without complex networking setup.

questions.question: A financial institution requires a network design that supports active-active disaster recovery across two regions with RPO of 1 minute. The solution must maintain session state and support database replication. What architecture should be designed?
options: Global Load Balancer with Route 53 health checks and RDS Multi-AZ
Route 53 Application Recovery Controller with cross-region replication
Global Accelerator with Network Load Balancers and Aurora Global Database
CloudFront with origin failover and DynamoDB Global Tables
questions.explanation: Global Accelerator provides active-active load balancing with health checks. Aurora Global Database supports cross-region replication with RPO < 1 second, meeting the 1-minute requirement.

questions.question: A gaming company needs to design a network architecture for a real-time multiplayer game supporting 1 million concurrent users globally. The solution must minimize latency and support UDP traffic. What design should be implemented?
options: CloudFront with UDP support and Lambda@Edge
Global Accelerator with Network Load Balancers and UDP listeners
Route 53 latency-based routing with Application Load Balancers
Multi-region deployment with local load balancers
questions.explanation: Global Accelerator optimizes UDP traffic routing using AWS global network. Network Load Balancers support UDP with high performance and can handle millions of concurrent connections.

questions.question: An IoT company needs to design a network architecture for 100,000 devices sending telemetry data. The solution must support device authentication and data encryption. What approach should be used?
options: Application Load Balancer with SSL termination and AWS IoT Core
Network Load Balancer with TCP listeners and custom authentication
AWS IoT Core with device certificates and MQTT over TLS
API Gateway with API keys and Lambda functions
questions.explanation: AWS IoT Core is purpose-built for IoT devices, supporting MQTT over TLS for secure communication and X.509 certificates for device authentication at scale.

questions.question: A company needs to design a network that allows their EC2 instances to access S3 without internet traffic. What solution should be implemented?
options: NAT Gateway with S3 bucket policy
VPC Endpoint for S3 (Gateway Endpoint)
Internet Gateway with security group rules
Direct Connect with private VIF
questions.explanation: VPC Gateway Endpoint for S3 allows private connectivity to S3 without internet traffic. It's free and provides secure access to S3 from within the VPC.

questions.question: A multinational corporation needs to design a network architecture that complies with data sovereignty requirements across 10 countries. Each country's data must remain within its borders. What design approach should be used?
options: Single global VPC with country-specific subnets
Regional VPCs per country with no cross-border connectivity
Transit Gateway with country-specific route tables and policies
Separate AWS accounts per country with cross-account roles
questions.explanation: Regional VPCs per country ensure data sovereignty by keeping all data within country borders. No cross-border connectivity prevents accidental data transfer across jurisdictions.

questions.question: A media streaming company needs to design a network that supports adaptive bitrate streaming with global content delivery. The solution must cache content at edge locations and support real-time analytics. What architecture should be implemented?
options: Global Accelerator with caching enabled
Route 53 with geolocation routing and CloudWatch
Multi-region ALBs with sticky sessions
CloudFront with Lambda@Edge and real-time logs
questions.explanation: CloudFront provides global edge caching for streaming content, Lambda@Edge enables adaptive bitrate logic, and real-time logs provide analytics for optimization.

questions.question: A startup needs to design a cost-effective network for their web application that expects low to moderate traffic. The application requires SSL termination and basic load balancing. What solution is most appropriate?
options: Network Load Balancer with SSL certificates
Application Load Balancer with AWS Certificate Manager
Classic Load Balancer with self-signed certificates
Gateway Load Balancer with third-party SSL
questions.explanation: Application Load Balancer is cost-effective for HTTP/HTTPS traffic with low to moderate volume. AWS Certificate Manager provides free SSL certificates, reducing costs.

questions.question: An e-commerce company needs to design a network architecture that supports seasonal traffic spikes of 10x normal load. The solution must automatically scale and maintain performance. What design should be implemented?
options: Fixed capacity with Network Load Balancer and manual scaling
Lambda functions with API Gateway and automatic scaling
ECS Fargate with Service Auto Scaling and ALB
Auto Scaling Groups with Application Load Balancer and CloudWatch alarms
questions.explanation: Auto Scaling Groups automatically handle traffic spikes by scaling EC2 instances. Application Load Balancer distributes traffic efficiently, and CloudWatch alarms trigger scaling actions.

questions.question: A financial services company requires a network design that supports high-frequency trading with sub-millisecond latency requirements. The solution must connect to multiple exchanges and support market data feeds. What architecture should be designed?
options: Dedicated hosts with SR-IOV and enhanced networking
Placement groups with cluster networking and DPDK
Standard instances with optimized AMIs
Spot instances with high network performance
questions.explanation: Placement groups with cluster networking provide the lowest latency within AWS. DPDK (Data Plane Development Kit) bypasses the kernel for ultra-low latency packet processing required for HFT.

questions.question: A healthcare organization needs to design a network that supports DICOM image transfer between hospitals. The solution must ensure data integrity and support large file transfers. What approach should be used?
options: S3 Transfer Acceleration with multipart upload
Direct Connect with dedicated bandwidth
VPN with compression and error correction
AWS DataSync with encryption in transit
questions.explanation: AWS DataSync is optimized for large file transfers with built-in data integrity checks, encryption in transit, and bandwidth throttling. It's ideal for medical imaging workflows.

questions.question: A company needs to design a network that allows their development team to access AWS resources securely from their office. The solution should be quick to implement and cost-effective. What approach should be used?
options: Direct Connect with private VIF
Client VPN with certificate authentication
AWS Systems Manager Session Manager
Site-to-Site VPN with customer gateway
questions.explanation: Site-to-Site VPN is quick to implement, cost-effective for small teams, and provides secure connectivity between office and AWS. It requires minimal setup compared to Direct Connect.

questions.question: A global enterprise needs to design a network architecture that supports zero-trust security principles with microsegmentation. The solution must scale to 10,000 workloads across multiple regions. What architecture should be implemented?
options: Security groups with fine-grained rules per workload
Network ACLs with subnet-level segmentation
AWS Network Firewall with application-level inspection
VPC Lattice with service-level policies and identity-based access
questions.explanation: VPC Lattice provides service-to-service connectivity with built-in security policies, supporting zero-trust principles and microsegmentation at scale across regions.

questions.question: You need to implement a Transit Gateway that connects 50 VPCs with selective routing between development and production environments. Development VPCs should not communicate with production VPCs. How should you configure the route tables?
options: Single route table with conditional routing based on tags
Separate route tables for dev and prod with no cross-propagation
Default route table with security group rules
Multiple route tables with overlapping routes
questions.explanation: Separate route tables for development and production environments with no route propagation between them ensures complete isolation. Each environment's VPCs associate with their respective route table.

questions.question: You are implementing a Direct Connect connection with BGP routing. The customer wants to advertise specific prefixes to AWS and receive only certain AWS prefixes. How should you configure the BGP session?
options: Use BGP communities and route maps on customer gateway
Configure allowed prefixes on Direct Connect Gateway
Implement prefix lists and route filters on both sides
Use AS-PATH prepending for traffic engineering
questions.explanation: Prefix lists and route filters on both customer and AWS sides provide granular control over route advertisement and acceptance. This ensures only desired prefixes are exchanged in both directions.

questions.question: You need to implement a VPC endpoint for S3 to allow private access from EC2 instances. What type of endpoint should you create and how should it be configured?
options: Interface endpoint with security groups allowing HTTPS
Gateway endpoint with route table entries
Network Load Balancer endpoint with target groups
Application Load Balancer endpoint with SSL termination
questions.explanation: S3 uses Gateway endpoints which are free and automatically add routes to route tables. Interface endpoints are used for other AWS services, not S3.

questions.question: You are implementing an Application Load Balancer that needs to route traffic based on HTTP headers and URL paths. The application has three microservices: user, order, and payment. How should you configure the routing rules?
options: Single target group with health checks on different ports
Multiple target groups with path-based routing rules
Network Load Balancer with TCP listeners
Classic Load Balancer with sticky sessions
questions.explanation: Application Load Balancer supports path-based routing with multiple target groups. Configure rules like /user/*, /order/*, /payment/* to route to respective microservice target groups.

questions.question: You need to implement a multi-region network with Transit Gateway peering. The design requires asymmetric routing where traffic from Region A to Region B uses a different path than return traffic. How should you configure the routing?
options: Use BGP AS-PATH prepending on peering connections
Configure different route priorities in each region's route tables
Implement route maps with different metrics
Use static routes with different administrative distances
questions.explanation: Transit Gateway route tables support route priorities. Configure different priorities in each region's route tables to achieve asymmetric routing while maintaining connectivity.

questions.question: You are implementing IPv6 in an existing IPv4 VPC. The application must support both IPv4 and IPv6 clients. What steps are required to enable dual-stack networking?
options: Create new IPv6-only subnets and migrate applications
Configure NAT64 gateway for IPv4 to IPv6 translation
Enable IPv6 on Internet Gateway only
Add IPv6 CIDR to VPC, enable IPv6 on subnets, update route tables and security groups
questions.explanation: Dual-stack implementation requires: associating IPv6 CIDR with VPC, enabling IPv6 on subnets, updating route tables for IPv6 routes, and modifying security groups to allow IPv6 traffic.

questions.question: You need to implement a NAT Gateway for private subnet instances to access the internet. What configuration is required?
options: Deploy NAT Gateway in private subnet with Elastic IP
Deploy NAT Gateway in public subnet with Elastic IP and update private subnet route table
Deploy NAT Instance in public subnet with source/destination check disabled
Configure Internet Gateway with NAT rules
questions.explanation: NAT Gateway must be deployed in a public subnet with an Elastic IP address. Private subnet route tables need a default route (0.0.0.0/0) pointing to the NAT Gateway.

questions.question: You are implementing AWS Network Firewall with custom Suricata rules for deep packet inspection. The firewall must inspect both north-south and east-west traffic. How should you deploy and configure the firewall?
options: Deploy in each application VPC with local routing
Deploy at Internet Gateway with inline inspection
Deploy with Gateway Load Balancer endpoints in each subnet
Deploy in inspection VPC with Transit Gateway routing all traffic through firewall subnets
questions.explanation: Centralized inspection VPC with Network Firewall deployed in dedicated subnets, using Transit Gateway to route all traffic through firewall subnets for both north-south and east-west inspection.

questions.question: You need to implement a Site-to-Site VPN with BGP for dynamic routing. The customer gateway supports BGP but requires specific AS numbers. How should you configure the VPN connection?
options: Use default AWS ASN (64512) and customer ASN
Configure custom ASN on Virtual Private Gateway and customer gateway
Use static routing instead of BGP
Configure OSPF instead of BGP
questions.explanation: Configure custom ASN on both Virtual Private Gateway (or Transit Gateway) and customer gateway to match customer requirements. BGP requires unique ASNs on each side for proper operation.

questions.question: You are implementing security groups for a web application with database backend. The web servers need to accept HTTP/HTTPS from anywhere, and database servers should only accept MySQL traffic from web servers. How should you configure the security groups?
options: Web SG: Allow 80,443 from 0.0.0.0/0; DB SG: Allow 3306 from web server IPs
Web SG: Allow 80,443 from 0.0.0.0/0; DB SG: Allow 3306 from web security group
Single security group allowing all required ports
Use NACLs instead of security groups
questions.explanation: Security groups can reference other security groups as sources. DB security group should allow port 3306 from the web security group, providing dynamic security as instances are added/removed.

questions.question: You are implementing a Global Accelerator for a gaming application that requires consistent performance and DDoS protection. The application uses both TCP and UDP protocols. How should you configure the accelerator?
options: Separate listeners for TCP and UDP, Application Load Balancer endpoints
TCP listener only with protocol translation
UDP listener only with custom health checks
Single listener with TCP and UDP ports, Network Load Balancer endpoints
questions.explanation: Global Accelerator supports both TCP and UDP in a single listener. Network Load Balancer endpoints are required for UDP traffic and provide the performance needed for gaming applications.

questions.question: You need to implement CloudFront distribution for a dynamic web application with user authentication. The application requires cookies and custom headers to be forwarded to the origin. How should you configure the distribution?
options: Cache all content with default TTL
Configure cache behaviors with whitelist headers and forward all cookies
Disable caching for all dynamic content
Use Lambda@Edge for all request processing
questions.explanation: Configure cache behaviors to whitelist required headers and forward necessary cookies. This allows CloudFront to cache static content while properly handling dynamic content with authentication.

questions.question: You are implementing Route 53 DNS for a multi-region application. The application should route users to the closest healthy region. What routing policy should you use?
options: Simple routing with multiple values
Latency-based routing with health checks
Geolocation routing with default record
Weighted routing with equal weights
questions.explanation: Latency-based routing automatically directs users to the region with lowest latency. Health checks ensure traffic only goes to healthy endpoints, providing automatic failover.

questions.question: You are implementing a private DNS solution using Route 53 Resolver. The solution must resolve on-premises DNS queries for AWS resources and AWS queries for on-premises resources. How should you configure the resolver?
options: Inbound resolver endpoint only with DNS forwarding
Outbound resolver endpoint only with custom DNS servers
Route 53 private hosted zones with CNAME records
Inbound and outbound resolver endpoints with conditional forwarding rules
questions.explanation: Inbound endpoints allow on-premises to query AWS DNS, outbound endpoints allow AWS to query on-premises DNS. Conditional forwarding rules determine which queries go where based on domain names.

questions.question: You need to implement VPC peering between VPCs in different regions with overlapping CIDR blocks. The application requires connectivity between specific subnets only. What solution should you implement?
options: VPC peering with route table modifications
Transit Gateway with inter-region peering
PrivateLink with VPC endpoints
VPN connection between regions
questions.explanation: VPC peering doesn't work with overlapping CIDRs. PrivateLink with VPC endpoints allows connectivity between specific services across VPCs with overlapping IP ranges.

questions.question: You are implementing an Elastic IP address for a NAT instance. The instance needs to maintain the same public IP after restart. How should you configure this?
options: Use Auto Scaling Group with Elastic IP allocation
Configure static IP in instance operating system
Use Network Load Balancer with static IP
Associate Elastic IP with the instance at launch
questions.explanation: Elastic IP addresses remain associated with instances through stops/starts. Associate the EIP with the NAT instance to ensure consistent public IP address.

questions.question: You are implementing a network architecture that requires traffic inspection using third-party security appliances. The solution must support auto-scaling and high availability. How should you implement this?
options: Network Load Balancer with security appliances as targets
Application Load Balancer with Lambda functions for inspection
Transit Gateway with security VPC and static routing
Gateway Load Balancer with security appliance target groups and auto-scaling
questions.explanation: Gateway Load Balancer is designed for third-party security appliances, supporting auto-scaling, high availability, and transparent traffic inspection with GENEVE encapsulation.

questions.question: You need to implement a solution that allows EC2 instances in private subnets to access AWS services without internet connectivity. The solution must be cost-effective and secure. What should you implement?
options: NAT Gateway with service-specific routes
VPC endpoints for required AWS services
Internet Gateway with restrictive security groups
Direct Connect with private VIF
questions.explanation: VPC endpoints provide private connectivity to AWS services without internet access. Gateway endpoints (S3, DynamoDB) are free, and interface endpoints are cost-effective for other services.

questions.question: You are implementing a load balancer health check for a web application. The application has a custom health check endpoint at /health that returns HTTP 200 when healthy. How should you configure the health check?
options: Default health check on port 80 with / path
Custom health check on application port with /health path
TCP health check on application port
HTTPS health check with SSL certificate validation
questions.explanation: Configure custom health check to use the application's /health endpoint. This provides more accurate health status than default checks and allows the application to determine its own health.

questions.question: You are implementing a multi-account network architecture using AWS Organizations. Each account needs isolated networking but shared services like DNS and monitoring. How should you implement this?
options: Shared VPC with account-specific subnets
Transit Gateway in network account with cross-account sharing
VPC peering between all accounts
Separate networks with VPN connections
questions.explanation: Transit Gateway in a dedicated network account with Resource Access Manager (RAM) sharing provides centralized networking while maintaining account isolation. Shared services can be accessed through the Transit Gateway.

questions.question: You need to implement SSL/TLS termination for a web application with custom SSL certificates. The solution must support SNI for multiple domains. Which load balancer configuration should you use?
options: Network Load Balancer with TLS listener and certificate list
Application Load Balancer with HTTPS listener and certificate list
Classic Load Balancer with SSL certificate
Gateway Load Balancer with SSL passthrough
questions.explanation: Application Load Balancer supports SNI with multiple SSL certificates in a certificate list. This allows serving multiple domains with different certificates from a single load balancer.

questions.question: You are implementing a bastion host for secure access to private subnet instances. What security configuration should be applied?
options: Place in private subnet with VPN access
Place in public subnet with SSH access from specific IP ranges
Place in public subnet with RDP access from anywhere
Use NAT instance as bastion host
questions.explanation: Bastion host should be in public subnet for external access but restrict SSH access to specific trusted IP ranges. This provides secure administrative access to private resources.

questions.question: You are implementing a disaster recovery solution that requires network failover between regions within 60 seconds. The solution must maintain session state and support database replication. How should you implement this?
options: Global Accelerator with health checks and RDS Multi-AZ
CloudFront with origin failover and DynamoDB Global Tables
Application Load Balancer with cross-region targets
Route 53 health checks with 30-second intervals and Aurora Global Database
questions.explanation: Route 53 health checks with 30-second intervals can detect failures and failover within 60 seconds. Aurora Global Database provides cross-region replication with minimal RPO/RTO.

questions.question: You need to implement a solution that provides dedicated network capacity between your data center and AWS with consistent performance. The solution must support multiple VPCs across regions. What should you implement?
options: Site-to-Site VPN with multiple tunnels
Direct Connect with Direct Connect Gateway
Internet Gateway with dedicated bandwidth
Transit Gateway with VPN attachments
questions.explanation: Direct Connect provides dedicated network capacity with consistent performance. Direct Connect Gateway enables connection to multiple VPCs across regions from a single Direct Connect connection.

questions.question: You are implementing network monitoring for a VPC to capture traffic metadata for security analysis. What AWS service should you enable?
options: CloudTrail for API logging
VPC Flow Logs for traffic metadata
CloudWatch for performance metrics
Config for configuration changes
questions.explanation: VPC Flow Logs capture metadata about IP traffic flowing through network interfaces, including source/destination IPs, ports, protocols, and traffic volume for security analysis.

questions.question: You need to troubleshoot connectivity issues between EC2 instances in different subnets. VPC Flow Logs show traffic leaving source but not reaching destination. What should you check first?
options: Security group rules on both instances
Network ACL rules on both subnets
Route table entries for both subnets
Internet Gateway configuration
questions.explanation: If traffic leaves source but doesn't reach destination, route table entries are the most likely cause. Ensure both subnets have routes to each other's CIDR blocks.

questions.question: You are analyzing VPC Flow Logs and notice a high volume of REJECT entries from specific source IPs. The traffic is targeting port 22 on multiple instances. What automated response should you implement?
options: CloudWatch alarm with SNS notification
Lambda function to update security groups and block IPs
AWS WAF with IP blocking rules
GuardDuty with automatic remediation
questions.explanation: Lambda function triggered by CloudWatch Logs can automatically analyze flow logs, detect brute force attacks, and update security groups to block malicious IPs in real-time.

questions.question: You need to monitor the health and performance of your Application Load Balancer. Which CloudWatch metrics should you focus on?
options: NetworkIn and NetworkOut
RequestCount, TargetResponseTime, and HTTPCode_Target_2XX_Count
CPUUtilization and MemoryUtilization
DiskReadOps and DiskWriteOps
questions.explanation: ALB-specific metrics like RequestCount (traffic volume), TargetResponseTime (performance), and HTTPCode_Target_2XX_Count (success rate) provide insights into load balancer health and performance.

questions.question: You are managing a Transit Gateway with 30 VPC attachments. You need to implement centralized logging and monitoring for all route propagation changes. What solution should you implement?
options: VPC Flow Logs on all attachments
CloudWatch Events for route table changes
AWS Config rules for Transit Gateway compliance
CloudTrail with Transit Gateway API logging
questions.explanation: CloudTrail logs all Transit Gateway API calls including route propagation changes, attachment modifications, and route table updates, providing centralized audit trail.

questions.question: You need to implement automated network path analysis to verify connectivity between specific EC2 instances across multiple VPCs. The solution should run daily and alert on connectivity failures. What should you implement?
options: Custom ping tests with CloudWatch synthetic monitoring
Network Load Balancer health checks with notifications
VPC Flow Logs analysis with custom scripts
VPC Reachability Analyzer with Lambda automation and CloudWatch alarms
questions.explanation: VPC Reachability Analyzer can be automated with Lambda to run daily path analysis between specified instances. CloudWatch alarms can trigger notifications when connectivity issues are detected.

questions.question: You are troubleshooting intermittent connection timeouts to your RDS database from EC2 instances. The database is in a private subnet with proper security groups. What diagnostic approach should you use?
options: Enable VPC Flow Logs and analyze connection patterns
Check RDS performance metrics and connection counts
Verify DNS resolution and network latency
All of the above in systematic order
questions.explanation: Intermittent timeouts require systematic diagnosis: VPC Flow Logs for network connectivity, RDS metrics for database performance, and DNS/latency checks for infrastructure issues.

questions.question: You need to monitor bandwidth utilization on your Direct Connect connection. Which CloudWatch metrics should you track?
options: ConnectionBpsEgress and ConnectionBpsIngress
NetworkPacketsIn and NetworkPacketsOut
ConnectionCRCErrorCount and ConnectionLightLevelLow
VirtualInterfaceBpsEgress and VirtualInterfaceBpsIngress
questions.explanation: VirtualInterfaceBpsEgress and VirtualInterfaceBpsIngress metrics show actual bandwidth utilization per VIF, which is more granular than connection-level metrics.

questions.question: You are managing a complex network with multiple Transit Gateways across regions. You need to implement centralized route management and prevent routing loops. What solution should you implement?
options: Custom Lambda functions for route management
CloudFormation templates with route dependencies
Manual route table management with documentation
AWS Network Manager with global network topology
questions.explanation: AWS Network Manager provides centralized visibility and management of global network topology, including Transit Gateway routing, with built-in loop prevention and route optimization.

questions.question: You need to implement traffic mirroring for security analysis of suspicious network activity. The solution must capture all traffic from specific instances without impacting performance. How should you configure this?
options: VPC Flow Logs with detailed monitoring
CloudWatch Logs with custom agents
AWS Network Firewall with logging enabled
VPC Traffic Mirroring with Network Load Balancer as target
questions.explanation: VPC Traffic Mirroring captures actual packet data (not just metadata) and can use Network Load Balancer as target for high-performance analysis without impacting source instances.

questions.question: You are monitoring CloudFront distribution performance and notice high cache miss rates. What metrics should you analyze to optimize caching?
options: OriginLatency and CacheHitRate
Requests and BytesDownloaded
ErrorRate and 4xxErrorRate
ViewerRequests and ViewerResponseTime
questions.explanation: OriginLatency shows how long origins take to respond, and CacheHitRate indicates caching effectiveness. These metrics help identify caching optimization opportunities.

questions.question: You need to implement automated remediation for network security incidents detected by GuardDuty. The solution should isolate compromised instances and preserve evidence. What architecture should you implement?
options: GuardDuty → CloudWatch Events → Lambda → Security Group isolation + EBS snapshot
GuardDuty → SNS → Manual intervention
GuardDuty → Systems Manager → Instance termination
GuardDuty → AWS Config → Compliance remediation
questions.explanation: Automated response using CloudWatch Events triggers Lambda function to isolate instances by modifying security groups and create EBS snapshots for forensic analysis while preserving evidence.

questions.question: You are managing DNS resolution for a hybrid environment with Route 53 Resolver. You need to troubleshoot DNS queries that are not resolving correctly. What diagnostic tools should you use?
options: Route 53 Resolver query logs and CloudWatch metrics
VPC Flow Logs for DNS traffic analysis
CloudTrail for DNS API calls
Network Load Balancer access logs
questions.explanation: Route 53 Resolver query logs show DNS resolution details, and CloudWatch metrics provide performance data. These are the primary tools for DNS troubleshooting in hybrid environments.

questions.question: You need to set up monitoring alerts for when your NAT Gateway approaches its bandwidth limits. What CloudWatch metric should you monitor?
options: NetworkIn and NetworkOut
BytesInFromDestination and BytesToDestination
PacketsDropCount and ErrorPortAllocation
ActiveConnectionCount and NewConnectionCount
questions.explanation: BytesInFromDestination and BytesToDestination metrics show actual data transfer through NAT Gateway, which helps monitor bandwidth utilization and set appropriate alerts.

questions.question: You are implementing a comprehensive network monitoring solution for a multi-account, multi-region environment. The solution must provide centralized visibility and automated alerting. What architecture should you implement?
options: Centralized CloudWatch with cross-account roles and custom dashboards
AWS Network Manager with CloudWatch integration and EventBridge rules
Third-party monitoring tools with AWS API integration
Individual account monitoring with manual aggregation
questions.explanation: AWS Network Manager provides centralized network topology visibility across accounts and regions, integrating with CloudWatch for metrics and EventBridge for automated alerting and remediation.

questions.question: You need to analyze network performance issues affecting application response times. Users report slow performance during peak hours. What monitoring approach should you implement?
options: Application Load Balancer metrics with target response time analysis
VPC Flow Logs with traffic pattern analysis
CloudWatch Application Insights with network correlation
Custom application metrics with network latency measurements
questions.explanation: CloudWatch Application Insights automatically correlates application performance with infrastructure metrics, including network performance, providing comprehensive analysis of performance issues.

questions.question: You are troubleshooting a Site-to-Site VPN connection that frequently disconnects. What CloudWatch metrics should you monitor to identify the issue?
options: TunnelState and TunnelIpAddress
VpnConnectionState and CustomerGatewayState
TunnelState and PacketDropCount
ConnectionState and BGPStatus
questions.explanation: TunnelState shows tunnel connectivity status, and PacketDropCount indicates packet loss issues. These metrics help identify VPN stability problems and network quality issues.

questions.question: You need to implement automated capacity planning for your network infrastructure. The solution should predict bandwidth requirements and recommend scaling actions. What approach should you use?
options: CloudWatch anomaly detection with custom Lambda functions
AWS Forecast with network metrics and automated scaling
Custom machine learning models with SageMaker
Static thresholds with manual capacity planning
questions.explanation: AWS Forecast can analyze historical network metrics to predict future bandwidth requirements, enabling proactive capacity planning and automated scaling recommendations.

questions.question: You are managing a global application with CloudFront distribution. You need to monitor and optimize performance for users in different geographic regions. What approach should you implement?
options: CloudFront real-time logs with geographic analysis
Route 53 health checks from multiple regions
Global Accelerator performance monitoring
Custom synthetic monitoring from edge locations
questions.explanation: CloudFront real-time logs provide detailed performance data by geographic region, enabling analysis of cache performance, origin latency, and user experience optimization.

questions.question: You need to monitor the health of targets behind your Network Load Balancer. The targets are failing health checks intermittently. What should you investigate first?
options: Target group health check configuration
Security group rules on targets
Network ACL rules on target subnets
Load balancer cross-zone configuration
questions.explanation: Health check configuration (interval, timeout, healthy/unhealthy thresholds) is the most common cause of intermittent health check failures. Verify these settings match application requirements.

questions.question: You are implementing a network observability solution that correlates application performance with network metrics across microservices. The solution must provide distributed tracing and network insights. What should you implement?
options: AWS X-Ray with VPC Flow Logs correlation
CloudWatch ServiceLens with network monitoring
Custom observability platform with AWS APIs
Application Performance Monitoring (APM) tools only
questions.explanation: CloudWatch ServiceLens provides service map visualization with distributed tracing and correlates application performance with infrastructure metrics, including network performance.

questions.question: You need to implement cost optimization for your network infrastructure. The solution should identify underutilized resources and recommend cost savings. What approach should you use?
options: AWS Cost Explorer with network resource filtering
AWS Trusted Advisor with network optimization checks
Custom cost analysis with CloudWatch metrics
AWS Compute Optimizer for network resources
questions.explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor provides specific network optimization recommendations, including underutilized load balancers, idle Elastic IPs, and Direct Connect optimization opportunities.

questions.question: You are monitoring AWS Network Firewall performance and need to track blocked connections and allowed traffic. Which logs should you enable?
options: Flow logs only
Alert logs only
Both flow logs and alert logs
CloudTrail logs only
questions.explanation: Flow logs capture all traffic (allowed and denied), while alert logs capture traffic that matches rules with DROP or ALERT actions. Both provide comprehensive visibility.

questions.question: You need to implement automated network change management that validates changes before deployment and provides rollback capabilities. What solution should you implement?
options: AWS Config with remediation actions and change tracking
CloudFormation with change sets and stack rollback
AWS Systems Manager Change Calendar with approval workflows
Custom CI/CD pipeline with network validation tests
questions.explanation: CloudFormation change sets allow preview of network changes before deployment, and stack rollback provides automated rollback capabilities for network infrastructure changes.

questions.question: You are troubleshooting performance issues with your Direct Connect connection. BGP routes are being received but traffic is not flowing optimally. What should you investigate?
options: BGP AS-PATH attributes and route preferences
Virtual interface VLAN configuration
Direct Connect Gateway allowed prefixes
Customer gateway BGP configuration
questions.explanation: BGP AS-PATH attributes and route preferences determine traffic flow paths. Suboptimal routing often results from incorrect AS-PATH prepending or local preference settings.

questions.question: You need to monitor SSL certificate expiration for your load balancers to prevent service disruptions. What monitoring solution should you implement?
options: CloudWatch custom metrics with certificate expiration dates
AWS Certificate Manager with CloudWatch Events
Third-party certificate monitoring tools
Manual calendar reminders
questions.explanation: AWS Certificate Manager automatically monitors certificate expiration and can trigger CloudWatch Events for automated notifications and renewal processes.

questions.question: A financial services company requires network-level DDoS protection for their public-facing applications. The solution must provide real-time attack mitigation and detailed reporting. What should you implement?
options: AWS Shield Standard with CloudWatch monitoring
AWS Shield Advanced with DDoS Response Team support
AWS WAF with rate limiting rules
Network Load Balancer with security groups
questions.explanation: AWS Shield Advanced provides enhanced DDoS protection with real-time attack mitigation, detailed reporting, and 24/7 DDoS Response Team support, which is essential for financial services.

questions.question: You need to implement a zero-trust network architecture that validates every connection attempt. The solution must support microsegmentation and identity-based access control. What architecture should you implement?
options: VPC Lattice with service-level authentication and authorization policies
Security groups with fine-grained rules per instance
AWS Network Firewall with application-level inspection
PrivateLink with VPC endpoints and IAM policies
questions.explanation: VPC Lattice provides service-to-service connectivity with built-in authentication, authorization, and microsegmentation capabilities, implementing true zero-trust networking principles.

questions.question: You need to implement web application protection against common attacks like SQL injection and XSS. The solution should integrate with your Application Load Balancer. What should you use?
options: AWS Shield for DDoS protection
AWS WAF with managed rule sets
Security groups with HTTP rules
Network ACLs with port restrictions
questions.explanation: AWS WAF integrates with Application Load Balancer and provides managed rule sets for common web application attacks including SQL injection, XSS, and other OWASP Top 10 threats.

questions.question: A healthcare organization requires HIPAA-compliant network architecture with end-to-end encryption and audit logging. The solution must support patient data segregation. What architecture should you implement?
options: Separate VPCs per patient group with VPC Flow Logs and encryption in transit
Single VPC with encrypted subnets and CloudTrail logging
Multi-account architecture with dedicated networking and comprehensive logging
Shared VPC with security groups and AWS Config compliance
questions.explanation: Multi-account architecture provides the strongest isolation for HIPAA compliance, with dedicated networking per account, comprehensive audit logging via CloudTrail, and encryption at all layers.

questions.question: You need to implement network access control that prevents lateral movement in case of a security breach. The solution must segment network traffic based on application tiers. What should you implement?
options: Security groups with tier-specific rules and no cross-tier communication
Network ACLs with subnet-level segmentation
AWS Network Firewall with application-aware rules
VPC peering with selective routing
questions.explanation: AWS Network Firewall provides application-aware inspection and can implement microsegmentation rules to prevent lateral movement between application tiers based on application protocols and behavior.

questions.question: You need to ensure that all network traffic between your VPC and on-premises network is encrypted. What solution provides the strongest encryption?
options: Site-to-Site VPN with IPsec encryption
Direct Connect with MACsec encryption
Internet Gateway with TLS encryption
NAT Gateway with application-level encryption
questions.explanation: Direct Connect with MACsec provides Layer 2 encryption for the entire connection, offering stronger security than IPsec VPN which operates at Layer 3.

questions.question: You are implementing a security architecture that requires all internet-bound traffic to be inspected by multiple security functions in sequence. The solution must support high availability and auto-scaling. What architecture should you implement?
options: Gateway Load Balancer with chained security appliances and auto-scaling groups
Network Load Balancer with security appliances in target groups
Application Load Balancer with Lambda functions for inspection
Transit Gateway with security VPC and static routing
questions.explanation: Gateway Load Balancer supports service chaining of multiple security functions with auto-scaling groups, providing high availability and transparent traffic inspection.

questions.question: A government agency requires network architecture that meets FedRAMP compliance requirements. The solution must provide continuous compliance monitoring and automated remediation. What should you implement?
options: AWS Config with FedRAMP compliance rules and automatic remediation
AWS Security Hub with compliance standards and manual remediation
CloudTrail with log analysis and custom compliance checks
AWS Systems Manager with compliance scanning
questions.explanation: AWS Config provides continuous compliance monitoring with FedRAMP-specific rules and can trigger automatic remediation actions when non-compliance is detected.

questions.question: You need to implement DNS security to prevent DNS hijacking and ensure DNS query integrity. What solution should you use?
options: Route 53 with DNSSEC validation
Private hosted zones only
Custom DNS servers with encryption
CloudFront with DNS caching
questions.explanation: Route 53 supports DNSSEC (DNS Security Extensions) which provides authentication and integrity verification for DNS queries, preventing DNS hijacking and spoofing attacks.

questions.question: You need to implement a network security architecture that provides threat intelligence integration and automated response to emerging threats. The solution must correlate network and application-level threats. What should you implement?
options: GuardDuty with custom threat intelligence feeds and automated remediation
AWS Security Hub with third-party threat intelligence integration
AWS Network Firewall with Suricata rules and threat feeds
Custom SIEM solution with AWS API integration
questions.explanation: GuardDuty provides threat intelligence integration, machine learning-based threat detection, and can trigger automated remediation through CloudWatch Events and Lambda functions.

questions.question: A multinational corporation needs to implement data residency controls to ensure customer data remains within specific geographic boundaries. What network architecture approach should you use?
options: Regional VPCs with no cross-region connectivity and local data processing
Global VPC with geolocation-based routing
Single region deployment with global load balancing
Multi-region deployment with data replication controls
questions.explanation: Regional VPCs with no cross-region connectivity ensure data residency by keeping all data processing and storage within specific geographic regions, meeting regulatory requirements.

questions.question: You need to implement network-level logging for compliance auditing. The logs must capture all network communication metadata and be tamper-proof. What solution should you implement?
options: VPC Flow Logs with S3 bucket versioning and MFA delete
CloudTrail with log file validation
CloudWatch Logs with encryption
Custom logging with database storage
questions.explanation: VPC Flow Logs capture all network communication metadata. S3 bucket versioning and MFA delete provide tamper-proof storage for compliance auditing requirements.

questions.question: You are implementing a network security architecture for a PCI DSS compliant e-commerce platform. The solution must provide network segmentation, encryption, and continuous monitoring. What architecture should you implement?
options: Multi-tier VPC with dedicated subnets, AWS WAF, Network Firewall, and comprehensive logging
Single VPC with security groups and basic monitoring
Shared VPC with application-level security only
Public subnet deployment with load balancer security
questions.explanation: PCI DSS requires network segmentation (multi-tier subnets), web application protection (WAF), network-level inspection (Network Firewall), and comprehensive logging for compliance.

questions.question: You need to implement certificate management for SSL/TLS termination across multiple load balancers and CloudFront distributions. The solution must provide automated renewal and compliance reporting. What should you use?
options: AWS Certificate Manager with automated renewal and CloudWatch Events
Third-party certificate authority with manual management
Self-signed certificates with custom renewal scripts
Let's Encrypt with automated deployment
questions.explanation: AWS Certificate Manager provides automated certificate provisioning, renewal, and deployment to AWS services, with CloudWatch Events for compliance monitoring and reporting.

questions.question: You need to prevent unauthorized access to your private subnets from the internet while allowing outbound internet access. What security configuration should you implement?
options: Internet Gateway with restrictive security groups
NAT Gateway in public subnet with private subnet routing
VPN Gateway with encrypted tunnels
Direct Connect with private VIF only
questions.explanation: NAT Gateway in public subnet allows outbound internet access from private subnets while preventing inbound internet access, providing the required security posture.

questions.question: You are implementing a network security architecture that must detect and prevent data exfiltration attempts. The solution should analyze network patterns and block suspicious transfers. What should you implement?
options: VPC Flow Logs analysis with machine learning models and automated blocking
AWS Macie with network traffic analysis
GuardDuty with VPC Flow Logs and automated remediation
Custom DLP solution with network monitoring
questions.explanation: GuardDuty analyzes VPC Flow Logs using machine learning to detect data exfiltration patterns and can trigger automated remediation through CloudWatch Events and Lambda functions.

questions.question: A financial institution requires network architecture that supports regulatory examination and provides immutable audit trails. What logging and monitoring solution should you implement?
options: CloudTrail with log file integrity validation and S3 Object Lock
CloudWatch Logs with encryption at rest
VPC Flow Logs with standard S3 storage
Custom logging with database replication
questions.explanation: CloudTrail with log file integrity validation ensures audit trail authenticity, and S3 Object Lock provides immutable storage required for regulatory compliance in financial services.

questions.question: You need to implement network access control that allows only specific applications to communicate with your database servers. What is the most granular approach?
options: Security groups referencing source security groups
Network ACLs with port-based rules
VPC endpoints with resource policies
Route table modifications
questions.explanation: Security groups can reference other security groups as sources, providing dynamic and granular access control that automatically adjusts as instances are added or removed from application tiers.

questions.question: You are implementing a network security architecture for a multi-tenant SaaS application that requires complete tenant isolation and compliance with SOC 2 requirements. What architecture should you implement?
options: Separate AWS accounts per tenant with dedicated networking and comprehensive audit logging
Single VPC with tenant-specific subnets and security groups
Shared infrastructure with application-level tenant isolation
Container-based isolation with shared networking
questions.explanation: Separate AWS accounts per tenant provide the strongest isolation for SOC 2 compliance, with dedicated networking, IAM boundaries, and comprehensive audit trails per tenant.

questions.question: You need to implement network security controls that prevent privilege escalation attacks through network lateral movement. What combination of controls should you implement?
options: Microsegmentation with security groups, Network Firewall inspection, and GuardDuty monitoring
Network ACLs with broad rules and basic monitoring
VPC peering with selective routing only
Application-level security controls only
questions.explanation: Microsegmentation limits lateral movement, Network Firewall provides deep packet inspection, and GuardDuty detects suspicious network behavior, creating defense in depth against privilege escalation.

questions.question: You need to ensure that all API calls to AWS networking services are logged for security auditing. What service should you enable?
options: VPC Flow Logs
AWS CloudTrail
CloudWatch Logs
AWS Config
questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail logs all API calls to AWS services, including networking services, providing comprehensive audit trails for security analysis and compliance requirements.

questions.question: You are implementing a network security architecture that must comply with GDPR requirements for data protection and privacy. The solution must support data encryption, access logging, and right to be forgotten. What architecture should you implement?
options: Multi-region architecture with encryption at rest and in transit, comprehensive logging, and automated data deletion capabilities
Single region deployment with basic encryption
Shared infrastructure with application-level controls
Public cloud deployment with standard security
questions.explanation: GDPR compliance requires encryption at rest and in transit, comprehensive access logging for audit trails, and automated data deletion capabilities to support right to be forgotten requests.

questions.question: You need to implement network threat detection that can identify compromised instances communicating with known malicious IP addresses. What solution should you implement?
options: GuardDuty with threat intelligence feeds and VPC Flow Logs analysis
AWS WAF with IP reputation lists
Security groups with IP blacklists
Network ACLs with blocked IP ranges
questions.explanation: GuardDuty analyzes VPC Flow Logs against threat intelligence feeds to detect communication with known malicious IP addresses and can identify compromised instances automatically.

questions.question: You need to implement secure remote access for administrators to manage EC2 instances in private subnets without exposing SSH to the internet. What solution should you use?
options: Bastion host in public subnet
AWS Systems Manager Session Manager
VPN connection with SSH access
Direct Connect with administrative access
questions.explanation: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager provides secure shell access to EC2 instances without requiring SSH keys, bastion hosts, or open inbound ports, using IAM for authentication and authorization.

questions.question: You are implementing a comprehensive network security governance framework for a large enterprise. The solution must provide policy enforcement, compliance monitoring, and automated remediation across multiple accounts. What architecture should you implement?
options: AWS Organizations with SCPs, AWS Config with organization-wide rules, and automated remediation
Individual account management with manual compliance checks
Centralized security account with cross-account roles
Third-party governance tools with AWS API integration
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations with Service Control Policies (SCPs) provides policy enforcement, AWS Config with organization-wide rules enables compliance monitoring, and automated remediation ensures consistent security posture.

questions.question: You need to implement network security controls that prevent DNS tunneling and other DNS-based attacks. What solution should you implement?
options: Route 53 Resolver with DNS filtering and threat intelligence
Custom DNS servers with manual rule management
Network ACLs blocking DNS traffic
Security groups restricting DNS access
questions.explanation: Route 53 Resolver supports DNS filtering with threat intelligence feeds to block malicious domains and prevent DNS tunneling attacks while maintaining legitimate DNS functionality.

questions.question: You need to ensure that all network traffic within your VPC is encrypted. What approach provides the most comprehensive encryption coverage?
options: Application-level TLS encryption for all communications
VPC-level encryption using AWS PrivateLink
IPsec encryption between all instances
Load balancer SSL termination only
questions.explanation: Application-level TLS encryption provides end-to-end encryption for all network communications within the VPC, ensuring data protection regardless of the underlying network infrastructure.

questions.question: You are implementing a network security architecture for a critical infrastructure organization that requires air-gapped security for sensitive operations. What AWS solution can provide the highest level of isolation?
options: AWS Outposts with local networking and no internet connectivity
Private VPC with no internet gateway
Dedicated hosts with isolated networking
Single-tenant hardware with custom networking
questions.explanation: AWS Outposts provides on-premises AWS infrastructure that can be completely air-gapped from the internet while still providing AWS services, meeting critical infrastructure security requirements.

questions.question: You need to implement network access controls that support just-in-time access for administrative operations. The solution must integrate with identity providers and provide audit trails. What should you implement?
options: AWS SSO with temporary credentials and CloudTrail logging
IAM users with permanent access keys
Security groups with time-based rules
VPN access with manual approval
questions.explanation: AWS SSO provides just-in-time access with temporary credentials, integrates with external identity providers, and CloudTrail provides comprehensive audit trails for administrative access.

questions.question: You need to implement network security monitoring that can detect unusual traffic patterns and potential security incidents. What combination of services should you use?
options: VPC Flow Logs, GuardDuty, and CloudWatch anomaly detection
CloudTrail and basic CloudWatch metrics
Security groups and Network ACL logs
Application logs and custom monitoring
questions.explanation: VPC Flow Logs provide network traffic data, GuardDuty analyzes patterns for threats, and CloudWatch anomaly detection identifies unusual traffic patterns, providing comprehensive network security monitoring.

questions.question: A company runs a multiplayer gaming application that requires sub-10ms latency for TCP connections from players in Asia, Europe, and North America to backend servers in us-east-1. The application does not use HTTP. Which service should be used to optimize global connectivity?
options: AWS Global Accelerator with endpoint groups in each region
Amazon CloudFront with a custom origin pointing to the game servers
Route 53 latency-based routing with health checks
An Application Load Balancer with cross-zone load balancing enabled
questions.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator is correct because it uses the AWS global network and anycast IP addresses to route TCP/UDP traffic to the nearest AWS edge location, then over the private AWS backbone to the origin — dramatically reducing latency for non-HTTP protocols. CloudFront is incorrect because it is an HTTP/HTTPS CDN and does not support raw TCP/UDP game traffic. Route 53 latency routing is incorrect because it only improves DNS resolution time, not the actual TCP connection path. An ALB is incorrect because it operates within a single region and does not improve cross-region latency.

questions.question: An enterprise requires Maximum Resiliency for their Direct Connect connectivity to AWS. Their on-premises data center is in a single city. What is the minimum infrastructure required to achieve the AWS Maximum Resiliency model?
options: Two Direct Connect connections at the same Direct Connect location using different devices
Two Direct Connect connections at two separate Direct Connect locations, each with two connections — four connections total
One Direct Connect connection with a Site-to-Site VPN as backup
Two Direct Connect connections at two separate locations with one connection each
questions.explanation: AWS Maximum Resiliency requires four connections across two separate Direct Connect locations (two connections per location), each terminating on separate devices. This protects against device failure, location failure, and fiber cuts simultaneously. A single location with two connections (option A) only achieves High Resiliency, not Maximum. A VPN backup (option C) is the Development Resiliency model. Two locations with one connection each (option D) is High Resiliency, not Maximum.

questions.question: A SaaS company needs to expose their internal service to 500 customer VPCs across multiple AWS accounts. The customer VPCs may have overlapping CIDR ranges. The company wants customers to have no access to their internal network beyond the specific service endpoint. Which connectivity model should be used?
options: VPC peering between the service VPC and each customer VPC
Transit Gateway with a shared attachment and route table per customer
AWS PrivateLink with an endpoint service backed by a Network Load Balancer
VPC sharing using AWS Resource Access Manager to share subnets
questions.explanation: AWS PrivateLink is correct because it allows the service provider to expose a specific service endpoint to consumers without granting access to the full network. It handles overlapping CIDRs natively since consumers connect via interface endpoints, not network-level routing. VPC peering (option A) does not support transitive routing, requires non-overlapping CIDRs, and grants broader network access. Transit Gateway (option B) also requires non-overlapping CIDRs and provides broader network access than needed. VPC sharing (option D) shares subnets, not services, and does not isolate network access.

questions.question: An enterprise is deploying an SD-WAN solution across 30 branch offices and wants to integrate it with AWS Transit Gateway for dynamic routing. The solution must support BGP and achieve up to 20 Gbps throughput per attachment. Which Transit Gateway attachment type should be used?
options: VPN attachment with BGP and ECMP across multiple tunnels
Direct Connect attachment using a transit VIF
Connect attachment using a GRE tunnel over an existing VPC or Direct Connect attachment
Peering attachment between the SD-WAN VPC and the Transit Gateway
questions.explanation: Transit Gateway Connect attachments use GRE tunnels over an existing VPC or Direct Connect attachment and support BGP for dynamic routing with up to 20 Gbps throughput per Connect attachment — purpose-built for SD-WAN integration. VPN attachments (option A) support BGP and ECMP but are limited to 1.25 Gbps per tunnel. Direct Connect transit VIF (option B) provides high bandwidth but is not the SD-WAN integration mechanism. Peering attachments (option C) are for connecting Transit Gateways across regions and do not support BGP or SD-WAN integration.

questions.question: A company's VPC was created with a /24 CIDR block (256 addresses). After rapid growth, they are running out of IP addresses for new EC2 instances. The VPC CIDR cannot be changed. What is the correct approach to add more IP address space?
options: Add a secondary CIDR block to the existing VPC and create new subnets from it
Create a new VPC with a larger CIDR and migrate all resources
Enable IPv6 on the VPC and use IPv6 addresses for new instances
Use Elastic IP addresses to extend the available address space
questions.explanation: Adding a secondary CIDR block is correct — AWS allows you to associate up to 4 secondary IPv4 CIDR blocks with an existing VPC, then create new subnets from those blocks. This avoids migrating resources. Creating a new VPC (option B) is disruptive and requires migrating all resources. Enabling IPv6 (option C) adds IPv6 addresses but does not solve IPv4 exhaustion for services that require IPv4. Elastic IPs (option D) are public IP addresses for internet-facing resources and do not add private IP space within the VPC.

questions.question: A company wants to prevent EC2 instances in their VPC from resolving known malicious domains used in command-and-control attacks. The solution must be managed, scalable, and require no changes to instance configurations. Which approach should be used?
options: Deploy a custom DNS server in the VPC that filters malicious domains
Configure Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall with a managed domain list to block malicious domains
Use AWS Network Firewall with a domain list stateful rule group
Configure security groups to block outbound traffic on port 53
questions.explanation: Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall is correct because it intercepts DNS queries made by instances using the VPC DNS resolver (Route 53 Resolver) and can block or allow queries based on domain lists, including AWS-managed lists for malware and botnet domains. No instance configuration changes are needed. A custom DNS server (option A) requires infrastructure management and configuration changes. Network Firewall domain lists (option C) inspect DNS traffic at the network level but require traffic to be routed through the firewall, adding complexity. Blocking port 53 via security groups (option D) would break all DNS resolution, not just malicious domains.

questions.question: A company is designing an IPv6-only subnet for new microservices that must be able to initiate connections to IPv6 internet endpoints but must not accept any inbound connections from the internet. Which gateway should be attached to the route table for this subnet?
options: Internet Gateway with a route for ::/0
NAT Gateway configured for IPv6 traffic
Egress-only Internet Gateway with a route for ::/0
Virtual Private Gateway with IPv6 BGP routes
questions.explanation: An Egress-only Internet Gateway is correct — it allows IPv6 traffic initiated from within the VPC to reach the internet but blocks all inbound IPv6 connections initiated from the internet, analogous to a NAT Gateway for IPv4. An Internet Gateway (option A) allows both inbound and outbound IPv6 traffic, which violates the requirement. NAT Gateways (option B) do not support IPv6 — they are IPv4-only. A Virtual Private Gateway (option D) is for VPN/Direct Connect connectivity to on-premises networks, not internet access.

questions.question: A global enterprise operates in 15 AWS regions and needs a centrally managed network with consistent routing policies, segmentation, and visibility across all regions and on-premises locations. The network team wants to define the global topology as code and get a unified view of the entire network. Which AWS service is designed for this use case?
options: AWS Transit Gateway with inter-region peering and Transit Gateway Network Manager
AWS Direct Connect with a Direct Connect gateway spanning all regions
Amazon VPC with VPC peering across all regions
AWS Cloud WAN with a core network policy defining segments and attachments
questions.explanation: AWS Cloud WAN is correct — it is purpose-built for managing global networks across multiple regions and on-premises locations from a single place. A core network policy (JSON document) defines segments, routing, and attachment rules, and Cloud WAN automatically provisions the underlying Transit Gateways and peering. Transit Gateway with Network Manager (option A) provides visibility but requires manual management of each regional TGW and peering. Direct Connect gateway (option B) only handles on-premises connectivity, not inter-region routing. VPC peering (option C) does not support transitive routing and becomes unmanageable at scale.

questions.question: A company wants to insert third-party network virtual appliances (firewalls, IDS/IPS) into the traffic path for all east-west traffic between VPCs in their AWS environment. The solution must be transparent to the application VPCs and support appliance scaling. Which design pattern should be used?
options: Deploy appliances in each VPC and configure security groups to route traffic through them
Use AWS Network Firewall in a centralized inspection VPC with Transit Gateway routing
Deploy a Gateway Load Balancer in an inspection VPC with GWLB endpoints in each application VPC
Use AWS WAF with custom rules to inspect east-west traffic between VPCs
questions.explanation: Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) is correct for third-party appliance insertion. GWLB operates at Layer 3 and uses the GENEVE protocol to transparently forward traffic to appliance instances, which can scale horizontally. GWLB endpoints in each application VPC intercept traffic and send it to the inspection VPC without requiring application changes. Deploying appliances in each VPC (option A) is not scalable and requires application-level routing changes. AWS Network Firewall (option B) is an AWS-managed firewall, not a third-party appliance insertion mechanism. AWS WAF (option D) operates at Layer 7 HTTP/HTTPS and cannot inspect arbitrary east-west TCP/UDP traffic.

questions.question: A company's on-premises firewall requires static IP addresses to whitelist inbound traffic from their AWS load balancer. The application uses TCP on port 443 and requires high throughput with minimal latency. Which load balancer type should be used?
options: Application Load Balancer with an Elastic IP assigned to each subnet
Network Load Balancer, which provides static IP addresses per Availability Zone
Classic Load Balancer with an Elastic IP address
Application Load Balancer fronted by AWS Global Accelerator for static IPs
questions.explanation: Network Load Balancer is correct because it natively provides a static IP address per Availability Zone (or allows you to assign Elastic IPs), making it straightforward to whitelist on the firewall. NLB also operates at Layer 4 with ultra-low latency and high throughput. ALB (option A) does not support Elastic IP assignment directly — it uses DNS names with dynamic IPs. Classic Load Balancer (option C) is deprecated and does not support Elastic IP assignment. ALB with Global Accelerator (option D) provides static IPs via GA but adds unnecessary complexity and cost when NLB already solves the problem natively.

questions.question: A multinational company must ensure that users in the European Union are always served by resources in EU AWS regions, and users in the United States are always served by US regions, to comply with data residency regulations. Which Route 53 routing policy enforces this geographic restriction?
options: Latency-based routing, which automatically routes to the lowest-latency region
Weighted routing with equal weights across all regions
Geolocation routing with records mapped to specific continents or countries
Geoproximity routing with bias values set to favor regional endpoints
questions.explanation: Geolocation routing is correct because it routes traffic based on the geographic location of the DNS query origin, allowing you to enforce that EU users resolve to EU endpoints and US users resolve to US endpoints — meeting data residency requirements. Latency-based routing (option A) optimizes for performance, not geographic compliance — a US user might be routed to an EU region if latency is lower. Weighted routing (option B) distributes traffic by percentage with no geographic enforcement. Geoproximity routing (option D) is based on geographic distance and bias values but does not enforce strict geographic boundaries required for compliance.

questions.question: A company hosts a public DNS zone in Route 53 and wants to protect against DNS cache poisoning and ensure that resolvers can verify the authenticity of DNS responses. Which feature should be enabled?
options: Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall to validate incoming DNS queries
